_comment: SPA history fallback. Without this, every route except / returns 404 on
Vercel: the CDN looks for a file at /feed, finds none, and 404s before
React Router ever loads.
Found 15 Aug 2026 by curling all eight routes against the first
production deploy — / returned 200 and the other seven returned 404.
Why it was invisible until the app was actually deployed, which is the
part worth remembering:
* `vite preview` and the dev server both implement history fallback
themselves, so every local check passed.
* In-app <Link> navigation uses the History API and issues no network
request, so clicking through the app never touched it.
* Once the service worker installs, ITS navigateFallback serves the
shell, so a returning visitor is fine and the bug hides.
That last point makes this the same shape as S21.11: it breaks only cold
loads and shared links — a report permalink, a shared filtered map view,
the PWA launching from the home screen. Precisely the arrivals the
product depends on, and precisely the ones a developer with a warm cache
never sees.
Rewrites run AFTER Vercel's filesystem check, so real files still win and
this cannot swallow /sw.js, /manifest.webmanifest, /offline.html,
/models/*.tflite, /litert-wasm/* or /icons/*. Verified by request after
deploying, not assumed.
Unknown paths also land on the shell, which is correct: App.tsx has a
`*` route rendering NotFound, so the 404 is the app's own, with working
navigation, rather than the CDN's dead end.

headers._comment: The service worker must never be served stale — a cached sw.js pins users to an old app shell and is the failure mode CLAUDE.md §4 calls out as taking priority over feature work.
Versioned filename (AI_MODEL_VERSION), so it is safe to cache hard and immutably. 5.2MB re-downloaded per visit would dominate the load budget PRD §10.1 sets.
